* [[African Union|AU]] officials report that [[Sudan]] has launched a major offensive in [[Darfur]], a day after it rejected [[United Nations Security Council Resolution 1706|UNSC Resolution 1706]], calling for a new 20,000 UN peacekeeping force. Over 20 people are reported dead and 1,000 displaced in clashes which broke earlier in the week. [https://web.archive.org/web/20070311044102/http://www.canada.com/topics/news/world/story.html?id=a7cd74a8-696f-4e24-852c-374f0d279a9e&k=405 (AP)]
* [[Mexican general election 2006 controversies|Disputed Mexican election]]: Deputies and senators of the [[Party of the Democratic Revolution|PRD]] occupy the stage of [[Congress of Mexico|Congress]] and prevent [[President of Mexico|President]] [[Vicente Fox]] from delivering his final State of the Nation speech. Fox later addresses the nation on an all-channel telecast. [http://www.phillyburbs.com/pb-dyn/news/88-09012006-706373.html (Associated Press)]{{Dead link|date=August 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} [https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2006/09/01/AR2006090100206.html?nav=rss_email/components (Washington Post)]
* Category 2 [[Hurricane John (2006)|Hurricane John]] makes landfall near the tip of [[Baja California Peninsula|Baja California]] at around 7 p.m. [[Pacific Standard Time|PDT]] (0200 [[UTC]] [[September 2]]). [http://www.nhc.noaa.gov/archive/2006/dis/ep112006.discus.019.shtml? (U.S. National Hurricane Center)]{{Dead link|date=July 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} [http://www.cbsnews.com/stories/2006/09/01/storm/main1961769.shtml (CBS)]
* An [[Iran]]ian passenger jet [[Tu-154]], ([[Iran Air]] [[Iran Air Flight 945|Flight 945]]) carrying 148 passengers crashes in [[Mashad]], [[Iran]] killing 29 people. [http://edition.cnn.com/2006/WORLD/meast/09/01/iran.plane.ap/index.html (CNN)], [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/5305750.stm (BBC)]
* [[Israeli-Palestinian conflict]]
** The [[European Union]] proposes new talks on the [[Middle East]] [[roadmap for peace]]. [https://web.archive.org/web/20070506120322/http://today.reuters.co.uk/news/articlenews.aspx?type=worldNews (Reuters)]
* [[Spain]] approves plans to deploy 1,100 troops to [[Lebanon]] as part of a [[UN]] peacekeeping force. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/europe/5306152.stm (BBC)]
* The [[Japan]]ese Vice [[Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry (Japan)|Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry]], [[Takao Kitabata]], says Japan has enough [[petroleum]] reserves to prevent an oil crisis if [[economic sanctions]] are imposed on [[Iran]] over [[Nuclear program of Iran|its nuclear program]]. Japan is almost entirely dependent on the [[Middle East]] for its oil and imports 15 percent of its total oil consumption from Iran.
* The [[2006 Zakouma elephant slaughter]] is the latest of a series of [[wiktionary:massacre|massacres]] which has killed off over 97 percent of the original (the year 1970) [[Chad]]ian [[African elephant|elephant]] [[Wildlife population|population]] of 300,000 animals. [http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2006/08/060830-elephants-chad.html (National Geographic)]
* Prime Minister of [[Poland]], [[Jarosław Kaczyński]], calls on the [[European Union|EU]] to develop a common foreign policy and build a "credible" military force. [http://uk.news.yahoo.com/01092006/323/europe-must-build-credible-strong-military-force-polish-pm.html (Yahoo!)]
* The [[Miss World 2006]] pageant officially starts with the arrival of 104 nations to [[Warsaw]], [[Poland]] for a month of activities across the country prior to the pageant's final on September 30th, 2006. [http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/articleshow/1951047.cms (Times of India)]
